To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel subgroup of human melanomas with overexpression of KIT and CDK4 that is not associated with known KIT mutations but is associated with high phospho-KT receptor expression.
we have identified a novel group of BRAF/NRAs wild-type melanomas that co-overexpresses CDK4 and KIT and that this group is sensitive to the KIT inhibitor imatinib.

(1) A subgroup of melanomas, which are not known to have BRAF or NRAs mutations, have high expression of KIT and CDK4; (2) These tumors have high phospho-ERk and are sensitive to Imatinib; and (3) Imatinib treatment of these cells causes increased apoptosis and G1 cell cycle arrest associated to inhibition of phospho-Erk and increased expression of P27(Kip).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a subgroup of melanomas that have KIT and CDK4 overexpression and are sensitive to KIT inhibition by imatinib.
the molecular basis for melanoma and the development of targeted therapy.
the identification of novel subgroups of melanomas with specific genetic and pharmacologic characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the KIT/ CDK4 over-expressing melanomas are sensitive to imatinibs and other tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) drugs and resistant to BRAF inhibitor drugs.
KIT is a novel and important therapeutic target for a subset of human melanomas, which is not responsive to BRAF inhibitors.

KIT/CDN4 co-overexpression is a novel subgroup of BRAF and NRAS wild-type melanoma, which is resistant to BRAF inhibition but sensitive to KIT inhibition, suggesting a role for KIT in the oncogenic transformation of this subgroup of tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
KIT/CDCK4 overexpression in a subset of melanoma cells is an important mechanism of oncogenesis.
a subset of human melanomas with KI/CDK4 overexpression is sensitive to imatinb, and that this subgroup may constitute a potential target for KIT inhibitors in patients with melanoma.
we have identified a novel subset of melanoma that is characterized by co-overexpression of CDK4 and KIT and that is responsive to imatinib.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are subsets of BRAF/NRas wild-type melanomas with high levels of KIT and CDK4.
KIT expression and activation is a potential target for the treatment of some BRAF/N RAS wild-type melanoma patients.
KIT/CDCK4-overexpressing melanomas are a unique subgroup with a potential therapeutic vulnerability that may be exploited by imatinib and other KIT-targeted agents.
